No. I. O. D. 803
Date...17...1...30.
January 10th, 1930.

- Soviet Agents -

Sir,

Reference to the attached the subject of Soviet Agents and Communists is a matter which receives our due attention, and necessary action is taken on receipt of reliable information. We have already been apprised of the possibilities of Soviet Agents taking advantage of the disturbances in North China to avail themselves opportunity to come through into China under the cloak of being refugees from the war area. The information given in this Dispatch shews that there is no definite information of the arrival in Shanghai of any of these Soviet Agents. In respect of the above we have no information of any arrivals here and due note will be taken by us of any new arrivals for observation and inquiries regarding their activities in Shanghai.

I beg to suggest that this file be submitted to our Foreign Section for information.

The communication from the Provincial Secret is based on the contents of an anonymous letter in all probability written by a Russian who anticipates this overt movement as the result of the release of a number of "reds" following the conclusion of Sino-Russian negotiations over the Manchurian question.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
PUB. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D. 813...
Date... 7... 1... 30.

Sir,

The arrival of Soviet Agents in Shanghai seems to be
the natural results of the negotiations entered into between
the Chinese and Soviet delegates at Nikolsk-Ussurisk on
December 3 and later on December 19 or 22 on one of which
latter dates a protocol was signed as a preliminary basis
for the ending of the Chinese Eastern Railway crisis.
One of the conditions in the protocol, which sets January
25 as the date for a formal conference to be held in Moscow,
provides for the re-opening of Soviet and Chinese Consulates
and trade missions in Soviet Russia and China.

The effect of this is likely to be felt soon in
Shanghai and in this connection information has been
received that a local Soviet sympathiser has been deputed
to find premises suitable for certain Soviet commercial
state agencies.

Our records also show that during December 1929
ten Soviet Agents arrived in Shanghai which number includes
N. Bourlakoff, Soviet Agent, who was arrested by the
Municipal Police on March 16, 1928 for communist activities,
subsequently handed over to the Bureau of Public Safety
and released from Soochow Jail where he served a sentence
of one year's imprisonment.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. L. O. D. 893
Date. 7 - 1 - 30
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai, December 31. 1929.

Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sir,

I have received Secret Instruction No. 7688 from the Kiangsu Provincial Government quoting Secret Letter from the Minister of Interior quoting Secret Instruction received from the Administrative Yuan quoting letter from the Secretariat of the National Government stating as follows:-

"Regarding the Secret petition submitted by the Shanghai Special Municipality as forwarded by the Chairman of the National Government, it related to a letter received from one signed Anti-Bolshevik stating that the secret Agents of the Soviets will soon come to Shanghai with the intention to start troubles in Shanghai and Nanking. This has a very grave concern with the peace and order of the districts. Orders have been received for the matter to be sent to the Headquarters of the Commander-in-Chief and the Administrative Yuan for circular orders to issue for investigations and apprehensions. Apart from having separate letters sent out, a copy of the original document is made and forwarded herewith for execution accordingly."

"Apart from having separate instructions issued, a copy of the original document is made and forwarded herewith and"

2.
you are hereby instructed to execute accordingly and issue orders in turn to the various Provincial Municipalities for orders to issue for investigations and apprehensions so as to end the troublesome origins."

"Apart from having separate letters sent out, you are requested to issue orders in turn for investigations and apprehensions."

"Apart from replying by letter and having separate instructions issued, a copy of the original document is made and forwarded herewith and you, the Shanghai Provisional Court, are hereby instructed to issue secret orders for strict and secret investigations and apprehensions."

Apart from submitting a reply, a copy of the original document is made and forwarded herewith and you are requested to give order in turn to the various Police Stations for strict and secret investigations and apprehensions so as to end the troublesome origins.

Shovin Tetsuo Ito,
President.

Chinese Section,
For thorough investigation
and comprehensive report. JH

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. Q. D. 803
Date.. 23..-12-29.

December 21, 29.

Sir,

I have to acknowledge, with thanks, receipt
of your letter of December 19, stating that you
have received information, through an anonymous
letter, that Soviet agents are planning to spread
subversive propaganda in Shanghai with a view to
creating disturbances, and to state that the
matter will receive attention.

Yours faithfully,

A/ Director of Criminal Investigation.

Mr. Shovis votsen Kou,
President Shanghai Provisional Court

Shanghai, December 19 1929.

Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council:

Sir,

I have received a letter from the Kiangsu Bureau of Foreign
Affairs quoting letter from the Shanghai Special Municipality
stating as follows:-

"A letter received from one signed Fan-
Foo-S-Hyi-Voo-Khab(?) states that there
are secret detectives coming to Shanghai
from Soviet Russia with their names ch-
anged with the intention to stir up trouble
in the districts and endanger the lives of
persons. It is requested that strict and
secret attentions be paid."

"It is found that
if the various points as mentioned in the le-
tter are correct, it greatly concerns the peace
and order of the districts. A copy of the ori-
ginal letter is made and forwarded herewith
with the request that strict and secret atten-
tions be paid."

"A copy of the said letter is
forwarded herewith and you, President of the
Shanghai Provisional Court, are requested to
execute accordingly."

Apart from forwarding a reply, a copy of the said original
letter is forwarded herewith and you are requested to give
order for strict and secret attentions to be paid and adopt

2.
precautions at all times so as to curb reactionary movements
and safeguard peace.

Shouin Votson Kou,
President.

Copy
Excellency,
I have knowledge that some new Soviet-agents are coming here.
Their task is to create disturbances here and at Nanking and
also other places. Now they know, that the small bolshevik-
slogans have lost most of their charm. But their interest is
less to spread communism as to spread disturbances. So they
are supporting every movement which leads to unrest. Naturally
the leaders in Moscow cannot send now notorious agents as
Borodin has been. So they have found new agents in the persons
of such Russians, who had no communistic connections before or
have been "White" Russians. They are mostly Russians or Russian
Jews from the border towns, especially from Kharbin. They have
received big sums of money and have all some acknowledged pro-
fession. They come here and to Nanking under the pretext to be
fugitives from the Russian War in the North. They have all
more money to spend than they could have by their previous
situation. This is the best sign to recognize them. Some are
women. Their leader, who himself, is a prominent bolshevik,
is still not here. So you must have a very attentive eye on
every Russian newcomer. They may come under a not Russian name.
Their presumptive leader will surely come under some German name,
and with some false passport.
Your Excellency will kindly excuse me if I write
anonymously but my life would be at stake, if the Soviet Spies
could know my name. And I know, that there are such Spies even
around you.
I have succeeded to make a modest existence for me
and my family and all could be lost if the Bolsheviks create new
troubles here.
Anon-Bolshevik.

2.
This affair is of far greater importance, than Your Excel-
lency can imagine. The position and even the life of every digni-
tary and nobly of Yourself is at stake. The care on every Russian
"fugitive" from Siberia especially of who are coming in the next
future. Don't let mislead you by any previous position. The Soviet
leaders have now expressly chosen persons, whose past and present
situation would put them seemingly beyond all suspicion. Enormous
sums have been distributed, and terrible catastrophes may ensue.
I cannot say more if I will not risk my own and my family's life.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

January 16, 30.

Sir,

I have to acknowledge, with thanks,
receipt of your letter of December 31, stating
that you have received information that Soviet
Secret Agents will soon come to Shanghai with the
object of creating trouble in Shanghai and Nanking,
and to state that this matter is receiving attention.

Yours faithfully,

Director of Criminal Investigation.

Mr. Showin wetsen Hsu,
President Shanghai Provisional Court.
